Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps:

- Deployment modes discussed: Hosted API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput & isolation), Private VPC/on-prem (for strict data residency & compliance).

Suggested PoC (high level):
- Duration: 4 weeks
- Objectives / success criteria:
  1) 95th percentile inference latency < 200ms at 5 QPS sustained
  2) End-to-end integration with your KV cache and minimal engineering effort to call inference APIs
  3) Demonstrate predictable unit cost (targeting X tokens / $ around your target 
 we can baseline after initial tests)
  4) Security checks: SSO, KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence review pass
- Proposed timeline: kickoff next week, baseline tests in week 2, scale tests in week 3, review + decision week 4.

Next steps:
1) I will send a PoC/trial plan doc with timelines and responsibilities (include SOC2 checklist).
2) Please confirm the internal stakeholders who will own infra access and security reviews.
3) Confirm whether you want us to run the PoC on Hosted first (fastest) or target Dedicated capacity from day 1.

High-level preference:

For the PoC, we are open to starting on Hosted to validate integration and then switch to Dedicated for throughput tests, unless Redwood recommends Dedicated from day 1.

Success criteria we care about (more detail):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 200ms for our baseline prompt set at 5 QPS
- Throughput: ability to scale to 20 QPS with acceptable degradation (for later tests)
- Cost: a rough estimate for cost per 1M tokens (we have internal thresholds to hit)
- Security: KMS integration for key control, SSO (OIDC / SAML), and SOC2 evidence review
- Integration: ability to use our existing KV cache and not require major changes to our inference path

Hi Sam / Priya 

Attached is the PoC / trial plan (redwood-poc-trial-plan-v1.pdf) and our SOC2 evidence checklist (soc2-evidence-checklist.xlsx). Quick summary below and some items to confirm so we can lock the kickoff: 

PoC plan (high level):
- Week 0 (kickoff): Introductions, scope, access provisioning (Javier for infra), baseline prompts + metric definitions
- Week 1 (integration): Minimal SDK integration or REST calls, KV cache wiring, and run baseline latency tests on Hosted
- Week 2 (scale): Scale tests up to 5 QPS sustained, then run step-up tests toward 20 QPS (Dedicated recommended for sustained higher QPS)
- Week 3 (optimize): Apply batching / KV caching / quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize to hit latency/cost targets
- Week 4 (validation & review): Final acceptance test, cost estimates, and handoff notes

Success criteria (exact):
- 95th pct latency < 200ms on baseline prompts at 5 QPS
- End-to-end integration with your KV cache and no more than 2 small code changes to your inference path
- Security: SSO + KMS proof-of-concept and SOC2 item list reviewed
- Stakeholder sign-off: Priya (infra/security) + Sam (product) + Javier (SRE)

Kickoff date proposal: 2026-07-20. Please confirm Javier's email for access; we will need a point of contact to create IAM roles and provide temporary credentials for Dedicated testing if you pick that path.

Notes on deployment modes:
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, we can run integration + baseline tests same day; less isolation but suitable for early validation
- Dedicated: recommended once you need predictable throughput or want GPU isolation; will require some provisioning time (1-3 business days for reserved pool setup)
- Private VPC / on-prem: used only if your legal/compliance team requires full network isolation and resident data controls; longer lead time and procurement steps

I can also prepare a short canary plan for Dedicated capacity to minimize risk during cutover. Attached plan contains a responsibilities matrix and the test harness commands Javier can run.

Let me know if the attachments don't come through 
 happy to post links.

Best,
Marissa Cole
